title: R' Shmuel (Jerusalem amora, student of R' Abbahu)

paragraphs: R' Shmuel. (An amora of the Jerusalem Talmud, a student of R' Abbahu.)[^4] As in Sanhedrin, end of chapter 1, where he said, "I posed it as a difficulty before R' Abbahu"; and in Avodah Zarah chapter 4, halakhah 1, he said, "I saw Rabbi Abbahu prostrating himself as was his manner"; he spoke in his name, as in Shabbat chapter 1, halakhah 6; Yevamot chapter 16, ס״הה [printed locator unclear].[^1][^2]

And likewise he spoke in the name of R' Ze'ira (R' Zeira), as in Kilayim chapter 2, halakhah 6; Terumot, beginning of chapter 4; Eruvin chapter 9, halakhah 4; Yoma chapter 4, halakhah 6; Shevuot chapter 1, halakhah 3, halakhah 6.

And it is possible that what they said in Niddah 15a, "R' Shmuel said in the name of R' Yohanan," is this R' Shmuel; but what we find in Pesachim 112b, "R' Shmuel said regarding a black ox," should read "Shmuel said," as in Berakhot 33a; דק״ס [abbreviation left unexpanded].[^3]
And we have already explained in the entry Shmuel that he too is sometimes called in the Yerushalmi by the name Rabbi Shmuel.

notes.text: The source’s רבע כארחיה is rendered ‘prostrating himself in his usual manner’. The complete prayer discussion in [Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 4:1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.4.1.5), Heinrich W. Guggenheimer’s Hebrew edition (De Gruyter, 1999–2015), discusses normal and sideways prostration and contains R' Shmuel’s report about R' Abbahu. This resolves the earlier untranslated ‘rava’ without altering Hyman’s Hebrew.

The printed Yevamot locator ס״הה remains unclear and is preserved literally. דק״ס is retained without asserting the earlier tentative expansion ‘Dikdukei Soferim’. Except for the Avodah Zarah passage noted above, the cited locations have not been independently verified here. Bavli period and colon are rendered as sides a and b; chapter and halakhah sequences follow the source without renumbering.

Hyman presents the identification with the speaker in Niddah only as possible. His proposed reading of the Pesachim passage and his cross-reference to the entry Shmuel remain attributed to him; no authority identity or link is established by this translation.

R' preserves an abbreviated title where this review has not established its expansion for that occurrence. The checked Avodah Zarah paragraph explicitly names Rabbi Shmuel and Rabbi Abbahu; “Rabbi Abbahu” is therefore used in that quotation only. The heading and other reports are not automatically assigned the same expanded title. The final phrase “Rabbi Shmuel” translates Hyman’s explicitly written רבי שמואל.
